tasks.short: Establish accessible classroom behaviour rules and apply them fairly.

steps.what: Choose behaviour expectations and individual accommodations
Prepare the accessible classroom rule sheet
Check the final rule sheet for meaning and accessibility
Publish the accepted rule sheet to the class resource area
Explain and practise classroom rules with pupils
Respond to behaviour and apply proportionate support

tasks.design: First test an accessible rule-sheet template in {DOCS}, populated only with expectations the teacher has chosen. After the teacher checks its final meaning and accommodations, the existing pupil learning environment in {OTHER} publishes that exact version; live practice and enforcement retain their time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule sheets are individually laid out and the chosen wording still needs professional judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document styles and approved symbol libraries can remove repeated layout work.
tasks.still_hard: Fair responses depend on the pupil and the situation.
tasks.human_edge: Know when apparent non-compliance signals distress or an inaccessible instruction.

ambition.what: Provide symbol-supported classroom expectations for pupils who cannot use the text sheet.

tasks.altitude: A little less time goes into page layout. Decisions about behaviour remain with the teacher.

reach.learn: Accessible document styles and the approved symbol vocabulary

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: accessible document templates can reuse layouts without choosing behaviour policy.

assumptions: Boundary is routine rule establishment, class publication and enforcement; disciplinary case recording belongs to its incident workflow and is not claimed as a saving here.
Shares are provisional task-design allocations, not measured baselines. Savings require existing rule-sheet preparation and class publication; no existing scheduled runtime counts.

The teacher produces expectation text, accommodation references and symbol choices in s1/s2. Fields are class_id, expectation_text, symbol_id, audience and version. Missing symbols are selected manually in s2, never inferred.
Test native template and versioned publication configuration before code. If the class environment has no controlled publication action, retain manual s4.
s3 approves the finished rule sheet, symbol meaning and class audience. Changes invalidate a1. Routine in-person responses are direct professional actions, not an automated release.
unknowns: Whether accessible sheets are currently prepared and published
Available publication controls and pupil access
research_questions: Does template use reduce layout time while preserving pupil understanding?

already_counted.description: Final accessibility and publication-audience check within s3

incremental.description: Maintain approved symbol mappings and test publication permissions

approvals.approved_version: s3 accepted rule sheet version plus class audience; edits revoke approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional: four points from the rule-card draft minus 0.5 upkeep = 3.5; half the draft benefit yields 1.5. Routine publication retains full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep pupil records accurate and prepare required pupil reports.

steps.what: Gather attendance, attainment and activity evidence
Enter new facts and corrections in a pupil record draft
Validate the final record changes against source evidence
Commit the accepted pupil record changes
Assemble the reporting period's pupil facts into the required report layout
Write contextual comments on learning and activities
Approve the complete report and permitted recipients
Send the accepted report to authorised recipients

tasks.design: Test the pupil record system in {OTHER} for native change approval, report templates and controlled delivery before adding code. Keep capture, contextual writing and final checks human; populate factual sections from accepted records and release only the checked report version to its checked recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts are copied from accepted records into separate report layouts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record queries, templates and delivery receipts can replace copying and repeated navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Observations require interpretation, missing evidence must be obtained, and recipient access can change.
tasks.human_edge: Explain progress honestly without turning observations into unsupported diagnoses.

ambition.what: Provide a source-linked term report with each factual field traceable to its pupil record.

tasks.altitude: The teacher spends less time moving accepted facts and more time explaining the pupil's learning. Assessment authority is unchanged.

reach.task: Specify a consistent pupil progress report layout
reach.learn: Field definitions, accessible reports and restricted recipient rules

evidence.claim: The supplied digest describes ParnasSys pupil records and learning-goal tracking; it does not establish the proposed approval integration.
Model knowledge: accepted structured facts can populate report templates without a language model.

assumptions: Boundary includes teacher-maintained records, report preparation and delivery. Lessons and original assessment are outside this task, without claiming their effort as saved.
Provisional shares require observation; only today's manual commits, report assembly and delivery earn saving. Already automated activity earns none.

s1/s2 produce pupil_id, date, attendance_status, assessment_id, score, goal_code, activity_note, source_id and record_version. Teacher enters missing observations in s2 at full time; no free extraction or automatic diagnosis.

Report requirements contain reporting_period, required_fields and layout_version, maintained by the school administrator; recipient permissions contain pupil_id, recipient_id, allowed_report_type and expiry, maintained by pupil administration. Setup/access work is in build_days; ongoing administration is separately priced.

s3 approves final record field values before s4. s7 checks complete contextual meaning, factual links, privacy and actual recipients after s6. Every changed record/report or recipient list invalidates its approval.
Prefer native configuration. If a report layout cannot be populated safely, retain manual factual assembly rather than assume an API.
unknowns: Which record/report actions are already native
research_questions: Can the configured report preserve source links and block stale recipient permissions?

already_counted.description: Check report field fidelity and recipient permissions within s7

incremental.description: Test field mappings and report layouts after record-system changes
Maintain report requirements and recipient-permission configuration

approvals.approved_version: s3 accepted record change version and target pupil record revision
s7 accepted complete pupil report version and permitted recipient snapshot

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional: 20 drafting points minus one upkeep = 19; half that drafting benefit gives nine. Record and message actions retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with families and professionals to develop an individual education plan.

steps.what: Read prior support plans and professional assessments
Contribute family priorities during the conference
Explain assessments and feasible support during the conference
Discuss needs and agree proposed goals with the conference participants
Write the agreed goals and support into a plan draft

loop.input: Teacher's captured conference decisions, prior plan and mandatory plan headings
loop.output: Plan draft with each proposed goal, support owner and review date linked to its conference decision
loop.check: Teacher checks every goal, accommodation, commitment and omission against conference decisions in s5, then approves the complete version in s6; no invented diagnosis or resource commitment
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; absent decisions or disagreement go to manual writing within s5
loop.why_not_simpler: First test native forms; free-text conference decisions still need coherent prose and distinctions between agreed commitments and suggestions. A template supplies headings but cannot safely express those distinctions.

steps.what: Approve the complete plan and its sharing audience
File the accepted plan in the restricted pupil record
Share the accepted plan with the permitted family recipients

tasks.design: Use the native support-plan form in {OTHER} first; add bounded drafting only for the teacher's free-text conference decisions in {DOCS}. The teacher still captures those decisions, checks the draft's full meaning and accepts the final version before separate controlled filing and family sharing actions; conference time is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans must reflect negotiated commitments rather than generic educational goals.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can organise actual conference notes under fixed headings, with professional review.
tasks.still_hard: Disagreement, sensitive support needs and resources remain for people to resolve.
tasks.human_edge: Hear family concerns and negotiate support the school can actually provide.

ambition.what: Give families a plain-language copy of the agreed support commitments with named review dates.

tasks.altitude: Less rewriting follows conferences; the teacher can spend that capacity on disputed goals. No additional assessment or funding authority is assumed.

reach.task: Check whether individual support commitments have a responsible owner
reach.learn: Plan field definitions and support-resource constraints

evidence.claim: The digest describes a NOLAI project to draft support-plan justification; it reports no results, so the proposed workflow remains a model-knowledge design.
Model knowledge: conference-based plan drafting requires checking actual commitments, not just field identifiers.

assumptions: Boundary includes the conference, teacher plan writing, filing and family delivery. Full pupil assessment and support delivery are separate tasks. Shares are provisional; focal baseline is 75 and outside participant labour is 25.

s2/s3 capture the family and specialist contributions before s4 agrees goals. s4 includes teacher capture of decision_text, goal, support_action, owner, review_date, disagreement and pupil_id; its full 35 share remains. Drafting starts only after these contributions and agreement end.
Professional assessments and prior support plans are existing artefacts produced in prior assessment work; missing or stale material is checked manually in s1. No model fabricates it.

Plan-sharing fields are recipient_id, pupil_id, permitted_scope and expiry, maintained by pupil administration; teacher checks the current snapshot in s6. Restricted system access and consultation on sensitive pupil data are in consent_and_access.
s5's 60% remaining covers all reading, decision-to-text checks and manual fallback at the assumed workable coverage. s6 occurs after the final revised draft; later changes invalidate both approvals.
Filing and sharing are existing manual actions, not new paperwork invented to earn saving. If absent or already automatic, their baseline and saving must be removed.
unknowns: Current plan writing and sharing process
Whether families or school leaders must formally approve the final plan beyond consultation
Permitted processing environment for support notes
research_questions: Can reviewers catch changed commitments and omitted family objections in a blinded plan comparison?

already_counted.description: Draft meaning and omission review inside s5
Final plan and sharing approval in s6

incremental.description: Review failed draft patterns and maintain plan headings

approvals.approved_version: s6 accepted education plan version and pupil record destination
s6 accepted education plan version plus permitted recipient snapshot

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional focal baseline 75: 19 draft points at 40 percent reduction gives 10.13 gross points minus two upkeep = 8.13. Roughly half the drafting benefit gives three. Filing and sharing retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Use specialised instruction to develop sensory, language, cognition and memory skills.

steps.what: Choose an appropriate technique from the pupil's support plan
Deliver and adjust sensory, motor, language or memory instruction
Record the technique, prompts and pupil response in the lesson note

tasks.design: Keep specialist instruction and the teacher's short response note in the pupil support system in {OTHER}. Evaluate its existing note form and plan view first; neither removes the need to choose the technique, observe the response or compose the brief evaluative note, so no saving is claimed.
tasks.previous_blocker: This task's difficult work is responsive instruction rather than moving existing facts.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technical enabler is assumed for this narrow task.
tasks.still_hard: A pupil's fatigue, communication and sensory needs change during instruction.
tasks.human_edge: Adjust pacing and support from the pupil's actual response.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the teacher's week or decision rights for this task.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: using specialised techniques requires responsive professional instruction; a record form alone does not shorten it.

assumptions: Boundary includes immediate method choice, delivery and its brief response note, with all note capture and save time in s3. Material development and formal progress reports are distinct tasks.

Provisional shares are not measured. s3 uses an existing short note form; there is no repeated report, recopying or outbound handoff inside it. If a longer narrative is required, assess drafting separately rather than treat this as zero by definition.

Teacher supplies pupil_id, lesson_date, technique, prompt_level, observed_response and next_adjustment in s3. A template can provide headings but cannot supply observations or interpretations; retain all capture and save time.
s3 is a direct human save: the teacher checks the finished note before committing within the same positive-time step. The gate is not an added separate self-approval process.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool, mapping or automated process is introduced.
unknowns: Whether note entry actually involves repeated copying or longer reports
Observed time spent accessing the support plan
research_questions: Does observation show a separable copying or report step that the existing note form can remove?

incremental.description: No new technical workflow to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Teacher-reviewed final instructional response note and pupil_id at save

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both a text-only short note and a structured short note require fresh observation and interpretation; instruction and direct save retain full time. No incremental upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Protect classroom instruction and family conferences while reducing accepted-record copying and plan rewriting.
reach: Help the instructional coordinator define accessible report fields and support-plan ownership.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who gives families clearer support commitments and traceable reports without reducing direct pupil support.
